item.title: New approach to strengthen dementia support for Islanders and families
item.description:
New approach to strengthen dementia support for Islanders and families jenniferdhogan Wed, 09/09/2026 - 10:38

The Alzheimer Society of PEI is developing a new approach to care supported by the province's 2025 Health Innovation Fund, to help families better understand and respond to behavioural changes associated with dementia. 

These changes can include repetitive vocal or physical expressions, changes in daily activities (i.e. sleeping or personal cares), verbal or physical expressions of risk, or changes in mood and personality. Often, caregivers are left trying to understand what is happening and how best to respond.

For many families, a dementia diagnosis can change daily life in ways they never expected. As symptoms progress, caregivers often find themselves navigating new challenges while trying to support a loved one and maintain a sense of normalcy. That is why more Islanders are reaching out for support.

In 2025, the Alzheimer Society of PEI served 1,108 Islanders, up from 737 in 2023. During the same period, the number of times Islanders turned to the Society for support increased from 3,030 to 7,076. 

“Doing this work, I have seen people struggle and be devastated by the disease, and I have seen lives turn around by having the appropriate level of support," said Jaime Constable, CEO of the Alzheimer Society of PEI. "Help can literally change people's lives."

The Alzheimer Society has spent the past several months working with a steering committee of home care leaders, geriatric specialists, clinicians, and other health-care partners to develop a more coordinated approach to behaviour support. Input received from clients and caregivers will also help ensure their new approach reflects the real experiences and needs of Islanders living with dementia.

As a part of this work, beginning this fall, all new and existing clients will participate in a behaviour screening process to help with earlier identification of changes that affect the quality of life and well-being of both the person living with dementia and their caregiver.

All families will receive education about behavioural changes linked to dementia and why they happen. Support will then be tailored to each person's needs. For those experiencing less significant changes, the focus will be on proactive, person-centred care including activity kits, social engagement and overall well-being strategies.

For families facing more complex challenges, they will be provided the opportunity for an in-depth assessment which will support caregivers in tracking responsive behaviours over time to identify factors that may be contributing, like the environment, needs, and preferences of the person living with dementia.  This information will inform personalized intervention plans, helping families and care providers monitor progress and adjust supports as needed.

The work is also strengthening collaboration across the healthcare system. By connecting with home care teams, geriatric specialists, clinicians, the provincial Dementia Specialty Team and other partners, the Alzheimer Society is co-creating clearer pathways to accessing help and support for people living with dementia and their caregivers. 

The Alzheimer Society of PEI is a registered non-profit organization dedicated to supporting Islanders living with dementia, as well as the family members and friends who care for them. Through counselling, education, support groups, social programs, and public awareness initiatives, the Society provides valuable resources and services to individuals and families across the province.

As September marks World Alzheimer's Month, with World Alzheimer's Day recognized on September 21, Islanders are encouraged to connect with the Alzheimer Society of PEI to learn more about available supports, access helpful resources, and to explore the enhanced behaviour support services offered.

item.title: Province reviews business supports
item.description:
Province reviews business supports jenniferdhogan Tue, 09/08/2026 - 15:16

Island businesses are invited to provide their feedback on how to modernize financial assistance programs.

In response to ongoing economic uncertainty and current trade conditions, the province is reviewing its suite of financial assistance programs for business delivered by Innovation PEI. To better understand the pressures businesses are facing, the province is hosting dedicated engagement sessions across the Island and launching another business feedback survey.

“Government’s job is to create the most favourable conditions for business to grow on the Island. We do this through tax credits, labour rebates, and non-repayable grants. Today’s economic realities call on us, more than ever, to ensure that our supports for businesses are flexible, and responsive not just to what they need, but to their potential for growth and expansion within our country and global markets as well.”

- Economic Development, Trade and Artificial Intelligence Minister Zack Bell

Innovation PEI will be hosting businesses in September to hear their feedback.

  • September 9 between 12:00-1:30 p.m. at Summerside Shipyard 
  • September 14 between 12:00-:30 p.m. at Mill River Resort
  • September 23 between 12:00-1:30 p.m. at Innovation PEI in Charlottetown
  • September 24 between 12:00-1:30 p.m. at the Rural Action Centre in Montague

Island businesses wishing to participate must register with Kathleen Townshend by email (kvtownshend@gov.pe.ca).

The survey will be open until October 9, 2026. Information from the survey will help inform how Innovation PEI can modernize financial assistance programs to better serve the Island economy.

item.title: Feedback wanted on annual minimum wage review
item.description:
Feedback wanted on annual minimum wage review jenniferdhogan Tue, 09/08/2026 - 14:36

Islanders are invited to provide feedback as part of the Employment Standards Board annual review of the minimum wage.

Under the Employment Standards Act, the board reviews the minimum wage each year and recommends future rates to government based on economic conditions and feedback from the public and stakeholders.

Islanders can submit written feedback until October 30, 2026, in the following ways:

  • By mail:
    Employment Standards Board
    Atlantic Technology Centre
    PO Box 2000
    176 Great George Street, Suite 306
    Charlottetown, PE C1A 4K9
  • By email:
    labourrelations@gov.pe.ca
    Please include “Minimum Wage Review Feedback” in the subject line.

Individuals and organizations who provide written submissions may also request an opportunity to make an in-person presentation to the Employment Standards Board. If you wish to make a presentation, contact labourrelations@gov.pe.ca or call 902-368-5550. 

Prince Edward Island's minimum wage is currently $17.00 per hour, the highest in Atlantic Canada, and is scheduled to increase to $17.30 on October 1, 2026, and to $17.60 on April 1, 2027. 

The annual review will consider future minimum wage rates beyond the increases already announced. For more information, click here.

item.title: Province launches Debt Risk Advisory Committee
item.description:
Province launches Debt Risk Advisory Committee jenniferdhogan Tue, 09/08/2026 - 12:49

Four Islanders have been appointed to PEI’s new Debt Risk Advisory Committee to provide strategic guidance to support sound debt management practices.

The committee is the final step in the province’s debt management strategy, implemented in 2025 to improve transparency and accountability in government spending. The committee will help the province identify, assess, and mitigate financial risks associated with borrowing, investments, and other liabilities. 

“Together, these professionals bring an extraordinary breadth of experience in finance, governance and strategic leadership. Their knowledge will strengthen our ability to navigate an evolving economic landscape, support sound decision-making and help position PEI toward sustainable growth.”

- Finance and Affordability Minister Jill Burridge

The four members are:

  • Jody Sanderson
  • David Arsenault
  • Christine Heldson Tekker
  • Craig Noonan

The committee will provide advice and recommendations to the Deputy Minister of Finance and Affordability on matters related to the province’s debt and financial risk profile, such as:

  • Reviewing and advising on the annual borrowing strategy
  • Providing guidance on debt portfolio risk parameters
  • Assessing collateral management frameworks
  • Recommending investment policies related to reserve funds
  • Supporting strategic initiatives and special projects as required

The committee will also contribute to shaping policy direction to ensure that financial risks remain aligned with the province’s established fiscal anchors and broader financial goals. These goals include maintaining a net-debt-to-GDP of less than 40 per cent, and an interest-to-revenue rate of less than 7.5 per cent and the establishment of a general reserve.

Committee members will be appointed for two-year terms, with the option to renew for a second term. 

 

Media contact:
Janice Fogarty
Department of Finance and Affordability
jefogarty@gov.pe.ca

 

Backgrounder

Jody Sanderson
Jody Sanderson is a seasoned financial executive with over 25 years of experience in global banking, capital markets, investment banking, and credit risk management. With a history including overseeing more than $250 billion in capital markets activity and $100 billion in credit exposure while advising governments, financial institutions, and major corporates on sovereign funding, debt issuance, and strategic transactions, he is the Founder and CEO of Sanderson Capital Inc here in PEI.

David Arsenault 
David Arsenault is a former PEI Deputy Minister of Finance, a Chartered Accountant, and senior financial executive with extensive experience in public sector finance, fiscal management, and professional services. He is widely respected within Prince Edward Island's business and public-sector communities for his expertise in finance, governance, and strategic leadership.

Christine Helsdon Tekker
Christine Heldson Tekker is a senior capital markets and infrastructure finance executive with more than 30 years of experience in lending, credit risk, debt capital markets, and investment management. She currently serves as an expert credit consultant to OSFI, teaches finance and business ethics at York University and UPEI, contributes to several corporate and non-profit boards, and is recognized for her expertise in infrastructure finance, governance, risk management, and public policy.

Craig Noonan
Craig Noonan is Chief Executive Officer of PEI Mutual Insurance Company, one of Prince Edward Island’s longest-standing financial institutions. As CEO, Craig is responsible for the overall leadership, strategy, and financial stewardship of the organization. In 2026 he was recognized as one of Atlantic Canada’s Top 50 CEOs and remains actively involved in initiatives supporting the Island’s business and community sectors.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
